record.summary: Two adjacent buildings on OCII plan block X4, tracked as one combined record since their geometries were merged 2026-09-22 (they share one DataSF Assessor block-lot pairing, mblr SF3940003, ~12m apart, not touching): UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, a 347,500-sq-ft, 12-story eye-care tower at 490 Illinois Street that opened November 2020 at a reported cost of about $237 million (SmithGroup architect); and 499 Illinois Street, a 6-story, ~450,000 sq ft biotechnology building completed 2008 and developed by Alexandria Real Estate Equities.

open_questions: MERGED 2026-09-22: this record combines the former mission_bay_490_illinois and mission_bay_499_illinois records, matching the geometry files' own 2026-09-22 merge (data/manual/mission_bay_490_499_illinois.geojson) -- both buildings share one DataSF Building Footprints mblr (SF3940003) and are described together as a connected 490-499 Illinois campus in commercial listings. UCSF's own occupancy at 499 Illinois St (leased, then purchased) versus outright ownership at 490 Illinois St is not distinguished by a source found in this pass.

Exact opening day within November 2020 (490 Illinois) is not given by the source found; only the month is confirmed. Exact month/day of the 2008 completion (499 Illinois) is likewise not sourced, only the year.

The 2006 construction permit's own block/lot for 499 Illinois St (block 3940, lot 001) differs from the lot the Assessor now uses for this address (lot 004); the address, biotechnical/medical-research-facility description, 6 stories, and $90M cost all line up with this parcel, so this is treated as a lot renumbering, not a different building. The permit's own completion sign-off (2009-04-06) also runs slightly later than the Assessor's 2008 year, which may reflect a lag between substantial completion and permit closeout.

2026-09-21 pass: found the January 26, 2017 Regents budget/design approval item for 490 Illinois St (UCSF calls it 'Block 33' in its own campus numbering -- assumed at the time to be a coincidental name collision with this project's unrelated OCII-plan block 33). The direct ucsf.edu article returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches in this pass; its content (matching $237,000,000 cost and 12-story/5-story/3-story massing figures already in this record) was confirmed via a search-engine summary rather than a direct read. A primary Regents PDF for the January 26, 2017 item itself was not located.

2026-09-22: the 'coincidental name collision' assumption above was reopened -- the owner directly identified OCII plan block 33 (data/records/ucsf_valley_center_for_vision_west.json, west of Illinois St, about 60-100m from this record's 490 Illinois St tower) as ALSO being Valley Center for Vision, not unrelated. Whether that west building is a second wing of this same facility, a distinct building sharing the name, or a misidentification, is unresolved -- see that record's own open_questions; not re-investigated here.
